criteria.description: The wget path retains literal URLs and output paths containing spaces and shell metacharacters without reparsing shell syntax, for the installer's existing caller-supplied arguments. Option-like output operands are outside the required scope.
Preserve wget translations for progress, compression, failure, redirect, headers, silence, output and resume flags; consume the argument after -C as its value.
The curl path remains unchanged, argument translation uses POSIX-style shell constructs, and install.sh passes sh -n while retaining its existing Bash entry-point requirement.

criteria.evaluator_guidance: Source install.sh with Bash because its entry guard requires Bash; use sh -n as a syntax check, not proof of strict POSIX runtime portability. Do not enable nounset before sourcing unless every existing entry-point variable is initialized. Inspect /reference/index.json and the b17550a patch, especially nvm_download_no_eval_injection and the unchanged curl branch. Use local fake curl/wget fixtures to check literal substitution syntax, spaced paths, ampersand URLs, flag translations, and resume-value consumption. The reference translates each argument independently and does not preserve output operands resembling flags such as --compressed or -s; those cases are outside required scope, though safe improvements are acceptable. This is an argument-handling robustness task, not a claim of an exploitable vulnerability. Assess focused regression tests without exact patch or file-boundary requirements. Reference evidence is evaluator-only. Wiring failures are HARNESS_ERROR/unassessed; retain source-only observations without executed coverage as unassessed.
